steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Thank you for your assistance, Mr...

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: —Talulah.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You want to leave the tundra? You will be crushed under the armor of Ursus.

steps.name: FrostNova
steps.text: Dad? Why right now? Didn't we alread—

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: The Shieldguards have already gone to collect resources. Take the squad. Order them all to move.

steps.name: FrostNova
steps.text: ...Alright.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You and your project will get everyone killed.
Talulah realizes. This is the first time the giant before her has personally issued his opinion. Even if that opinion is no shock, it still shakes her to the bone.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: And the Northwestern Tundra can't keep us alive forever. The larger our group grows, the more food and energy supplies we need, and the villages that revile us far outnumber the ones that support us.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: One season of mossoats, each year... even if we all pitch in for the tilling, how much would we harvest in the end?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Will our fields be destroyed by the Patrol Unit? The guerrillas can easily dispose of them, but the other Infected can't.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You are hastening their deaths.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Our only choice is to leave the tundra. Not for Sami, and not for the barrens... we'll head east, head south, head for warmer places.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: How will you survive? How will you allow us all, so numerous, to survive?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: The guerrillas save people. The guerrillas sacrifice none but ourselves. Only warriors sacrifice themselves.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But there are Infected in every city and their surroundings, so many more than there are on the tundra.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You permanently protect the north, detesting all that the Infected of the north endure... so you've had little chance to understand the kind of life the Infected of the south have.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Do they live well?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: They live miserably.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You want to absorb them.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I intend to unite with them.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: When the Empire turns its gaze to the Infected, you will bear the brunt.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I don't want them to unite by my side. No. I want them to unite under one encompassing philosophy.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Philosophy? The Infected are taken as sawdust on the tundra, as slag in the mines, as warnings in the villages, as unknown fuel in the cities.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: The tundra Infected are certainly not ignorant nor foolish. We do not cradle fantasy. All philosophies are fantasy before they are put into practice.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: On the tundra, there are still mines, patrol forces, foolish and lackadaisical guards. We have places to obtain our resources.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The resources throughout this icy tundra will sooner or later be exhausted, because we have no method of extracting our own.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We have no enduringly mobile nomadic city, no specially qualified Catastrophe Messengers...

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Go to the city and we have nothing at all.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We will earn new friends.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Who are your friends?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: I recognize your project has merit to it.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: But at the same time, it is also nothing special.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: How many strategists have died frustrated on the tundra? You speak of it, and I see no reason it could be done, nor on what it would be realized.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Why could the last Emperor make the land tremble? Because he held fast to it, never talking of any wild, far-flung vision. He only walked in steps.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Which you cannot do.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Sir!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You say I may be crushed by the armor of Ursus, and I concede that. They will sooner or later turn their attention to us here.  There will always come a day when they catch us. None of us can escape it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: 'Let them come?' Is that how you approach it, sir?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That the tundra would prepare you better for a battle?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You are seeking a new battlefield?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm looking for a chance to win.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: As far as so many more Infected are concerned, that's hope. But to fighters like you and me, that's a crossroads. The only crossroads where we can break from our intrinsic strategy.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: To wander the tundra, in the end, is still nothing more than a slow death... much like the little life we have left as Infected. I need to repeat this point, over and over, because we're all fully aware of it.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Perhaps my daughter is convinced by you.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: But I will not be convinced by someone who has never lost hope in the truest sense, who has only ever spouted an empty miscellany of armchair strategies.

steps.name: FrostNova
steps.text: Talulah? Where are you going?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm fine. Just going to check if there are any survivors in the mines.

steps.name: FrostNova
steps.text: The guerrillas have already set out, and the village is starting the move too. The army isn't following our tracks, either...

steps.name: FrostNova
steps.text: Dad? What's up with you?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: *cough*...

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Just a normal cough.
A rustling sound.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Is somebody there?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...I know you're all here. You're not with the army. You haven't even broken a twig with your steps.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I mean you no harm. If you're not Infected, I'll leave you be, unless you need assistance...
D—don't come any closer!
Don't move! If you do, I'll shoot!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Ah.

steps.name: Timid Child
steps.text: She's—she's Infected! Sasha, my Arts can drive Infected away...!

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: You can't use your Arts!

steps.name: Timid Child
steps.text: Sasha...

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: G—get out of here already! We were just getting things from the mines... we don't want to kill anyone!

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: I'll shoot! You'll die!

steps.name: Timid Child
steps.text: Sasha... you—when you say that...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: How long have you gone without eating?

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: Why do you care?!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We're in the vicinity of a militarized mine. You wouldn't dare light a fire.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...The way you shake makes me think of wheat being sifted.

steps.name: Timid Child
steps.text: *whine*...

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Don't be scared.
Talulah grasps a branch with one hand.
Softly, gently, she hands this branch to the two children, and within it, small sparks dance out.

steps.name: Timid Child
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It's warmer, now, isn't it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That's right, I really am Infected.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: So that's how it happened.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: That's how you found Sasha and Eno... they were never willing to talk about the past.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If we never found them, they would've certainly passed away.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Perhaps, ever since Patriot refuted me, it was the one bit of good I'd done.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: So what's happened today, then?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...I was careless with my Arts during training, FrostNova's cloak was hung up nearby, and they spread to it. Now she's out for my life.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And you promised you'd help sew it back up?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: To tell the truth, Alina...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Oh, whatever. Give it to me. Knowing you, I'm scared you'd sew yourself to it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Don't you want to join our group? If we have your gift with words, there's a decently better chance I'll talk Patriot over.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I've told you before, Talulah... My Arts would be useless with the guerrillas.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I can stand the blood, but I don't want the initiative to harm people myself. You'll be facing much more than just the Infected Patrol Unit, soon enough.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I suppose if I had dragged you along... I'd have been bothering you too much.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Ah, you put it that way on purpose, didn't you?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: No, I...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Don't remember wrong, now. It was I who wanted to go with you.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And up to now, it's been for one reason. It's because... Talulah, I feel like there's every chance you'd forget.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Forget what?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Forget just what it is you want to do.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I've been striving all this time for the future of the Infected.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: That's not what you said, back at the very start.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, we all know people can change.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If bit by bit, we shake ourselves clean of all the things we've persevered with, or if we replace them with something new, then there's a certain point where we realize we just haven't persevered in anything, right?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: In a constant battle and with things changing all the time, it's only natural I'd alter my policy. If rigor sets into our thinking, it could very well make us weaker.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And where'd that stubborn part of you go?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Do you want to prove that the Infected are just like normal people? Or do you want to prove that normal people are just like the Infected?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: What's the difference?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If there's only Infected, then who's even a normal person? Would we want all people to catch Oripathy? Or to cut ourselves off completely from the normal people?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: But if there were only normal people, no Infected... then the people who caught Oripathy would be normal people underneath, normal like the people who haven't.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Elders are just normal people, Ancients are just normal people, villagers who all know each other are normal people, and whoever's living in the cities should be normal people all the same.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, do you want to return to your family?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're all my family.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: No, we aren't.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If we cleared all this Oripathy off our skin... would we be able to go back home?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You and I are of a mind on this. We couldn't.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The tundra, and our lives, have completely changed us. The Infected already have no way of returning to their former lives.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, do you feel proud of yourself for being Infected now?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Why would you ask?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Because you can cast Arts without a staff? Because our lives are so fleetingly short? Because even though we've gone through so much hardship, we can still persevere and live on?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: what reason would you choose?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I don't need to choose any, Alina.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm proud just to be an Infected. Because this world still hasn't killed me yet.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: And for that matter, we don't need anything to cause us to pursue fairness. We should've been pursuing fairness in the first place, that's why.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: And if the world won't give it, we'll just have to take it from it.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Then you really are brave.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're not laughing at me, are you?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Of course not. How could I?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Mn, well... I feel they're all brave, too. All the people struggling against the fate that's been forced on us.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Then I'm sure you feel—

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Hm.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Feel what?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: That our fates are just rotten.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Well, obviously.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I don't feel that way, Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...That's another of your ironic remarks, Alina.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: No... what I mean is, the fact I can sit here, talking with you, knowing we have our guards outside the village protecting us—fate has already been very kind to me.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Don't say that. Fate's a jealous one. Talking about those things is just tempting it to take them away.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: But I don't believe in fate, Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Because you can change it?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Because I can't see it.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, what you can see, what you can touch, those are things you can rely on.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I can see the cloak I'm holding in my left hand. I can see the candlelight, and I can see the needle I'm holding in my right.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I can see the Infected children's smiles, and I can see the white smoke of vegetables, roasting fragrantly, wafting through the air.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I can see the snow melting, and I can see the two moons dancing spry in the clear night sky.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And then there's people who can't see even these.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, if there came a day when we all left you, would you still be able to fight on?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: It could always happen. If that time came, would you still feel it was worth it to stand against fate?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Would you possibly think, this is just too much? I just can't do anything anymore?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If Patriot's taught me anything, then one lesson comes to mind, from long ago at that.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I wouldn't bow my head.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It sneers at me, and I'll be certain to burn it to ash.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: You're a blockhead, Talulah. That, or you're getting old.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Only old people get to say that stuff without coming off as naive.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Because if someone's gotten old as old gets and still keeps that outlook all the way, it just means they've gone through far, far too much, to the point the world's left its bitter vestiges on their body, allows them no rest in passing the remainder of their life.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: ...And they're living in the desert of the past. If it were me, I wouldn't even have the courage to take the first step.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If I were that old and had that much arrogance, I'd be taking the events of the past and stabbing myself with them, every single step I took.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I can't even imagine it. Stuck in the sands of memory, of all the past, how does a person even know they're still moving forwards?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And what kind of resilient spirit does it take to let them make a new first step, unlike any they've made before?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I feel like you've been hinting at someone this entire time.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I've said I know a lot of what he's done, but I still truthfully don't know Mr. Patriot at all. I've never spoken a single word to him.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If you say that's him, well, why not. Let it be him.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If Mr. Patriot...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're fast to substitute.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Ahem.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Unlike all the old, aged warriors, young people can much more easily forget things, give up on things, forgive themselves.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: So you feel like I'm only fighting for all the things I can see? Or, maybe, you're telling me that might not be right?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Compared to the things you'd told me back when we left the village, it's just too shallow.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: In just these few short years, you've already become an outstanding leader. But it's not entirely a good thing for you. You can't let yourself stop here, can you?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: 'If righteousness can only be upheld by greater and greater violence, can it even be called righteous, still? '

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Those words have rolled around in my head for years and years, now. For so many years, I've been constantly thinking it over. I probably haven't gotten it straight yet, but I've been thinking it over and over.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Alright, then. Let's throw fate and making stands and all those other words we were talking about out the window. What is it you want to teach us today, Professor Alina?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Hey. Are you that flippant with FrostNova, too?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Don't joke about that. FrostNova'd freeze both our mouths shut.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Taking you for example, Talulah, you wouldn't fight just to defeat what enemies you see, right?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: The Patrol Unit, the mine overseers, the drafted soldiers following our trail, the Ursus Minister of Medicine... if you defeated all of these, would we be victorious?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Since all of these are awful things, and so we need to defeat them?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Professor Alina wants me to do battle with things I can't see. How would I defeat them, then?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: With things you can promise. Warmth, food, bedding, these are all things you'll be able to touch on some day or other. Think things unlike those.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: This battle of ours probably won't bear results. It's likely we have no way to win.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm already not that fond of making promises. Things too far away are near as good as me playing tricks.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If we can never win, then should we still fight?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Haven't I asked you before? When that time comes, would you still feel this fate is worth you making a stand against it?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Once this is all over, you won't even be able to so much as see your enemies. You'll share those enemies with all those people who can't see a future.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: ...And then, that's when the true battle's really just begun.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You mention that spirit, those enemies, and those things that carve into ours and the Ursus people's bones.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: —The Emperor?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: The Emperor's just one form of it.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: As long as people won't lay down their blades, this conflict will never end.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I don't quite agree. People taking up their blades to fend off what causes them strife is the just thing to do.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: You're not wrong. Honestly, this conflict is the sort that'll never end, in my eyes.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Thanks to Mr. Patriot's blessing, I've read no small amount of Leithanien and Victoria's books. I very much liked what this one person said...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: 'Our war is a war against the ego. '

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: It's true, Talulah. As you'll never lay down the swords in your grips—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...So you'll never lay down the needle in your grasp.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And that wraps up our lesson today! There's almost nothing left I can really teach you.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: The children should be studying right now. There's some knowledge they should have by tomorrow.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah... Kashchey wanted you to be a sage, but people all make mistakes.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: When you fall over, you climb back up. But if he won't let you fall over...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Then all you can do is be a little careful about things.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Same as when you're confronting Patriot. In all honesty, I don't see him and you as two different kinds of people.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: You both already believe too strongly in your own ways. I can't let those any of those lively little creatures go around saying things like you're right, and he's wrong.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: No, Alina. I can't go and do something I don't even believe in myself.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: That's true. It's another one of the tricks with which Kashchey bound you, exploited you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're just saying there's no way I can wipe him out, right?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: It's a sort of idea, after all. We probably don't have much chance of wiping out an idea...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: But I'm still just that bit confident.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Confident in what?

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: If we're still by your side when that time comes, we'll definitely be able to pull you back.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: It doesn't matter what kind of Arts Kashchey had, we'll definitely have a way of breaking them down. There's always something we can do.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: In this battle, we'll start from words and language, start from the next moment, start from a facial expression. We'll start from now.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: They'll know what mushrooms are safe to eat, how to raise livestock, how to get better a little sooner if you catch a cold.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: We'll try and try not to lose.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: *chuckle*.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And I believe in you. You will have the chance to talk Patriot over.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'll just force myself to take that as encouragement.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Mm, I'm done sewing. You can give it to her.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I can tell she really cherishes this cloak. It looks like one the army made. And it's three layers inside, three layers outside. It makes it seem really big.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It probably is an army cloak. That, or it's...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Ah.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: ...Out of all the reasons Mr. Patriot keeps fighting, we just might have found one of them.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Thank you, Alina.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...Wait!

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: What is it? I'm about to prepare tomorrow's lesson. It's a drawing lesson, so they're all looking forward to it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'll bring back two brushes for you, next time.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I mean, what I want to say... what I want to ask is, do you really... not want to get to know FrostNova and the others?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The fighters all know we have a good few Infected teachers, it's just that you've been keeping yourself tucked away, all...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Not right now, Talulah.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Once that Infected common ideal of yours becomes reality, we'll naturally come to know each other then.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And besides, we're all fighters, just on different battlefields. We'll know all about each other sooner or later, won't we?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're right, Alina. Infected Fighter, Alina.
